body.summary: Ran the full sweep in per-directory foreground chunks and hardened the suite against parallel-load flakiness. The retry-EEXIST test's child-process racer was structurally descheduled at its readiness pipe write (the write that wakes the competitor), losing the 50us retry window under load (measured 25% win rate, full budget exhaustion in 2/10 runs); it now uses four worker-thread racers that never block between reporting spinning and the window, verified 12/12 under the full-parallel src/shared suite that reproduced the flake, plus a self-healing daemonLog mode fixture for sweep runs killed mid-log-write-failure. The sweep surfaced exactly two assertions of the old fail-closed contract (dead owner -> refused restart): the control-script orphan-guard scenario and the shutdown-lifecycle-evidence guard-death scenario; both now assert the story's contract (quarantine with byte-identical record, restart proceeds like the healthy control). Every remaining sweep failure was re-run at the pre-story baseline (worktree at 24b73cdfe) with identical failure sets - zero story-caused failures. The sweep itself does not exit clean on this v2 baseline: ~130 pre-existing failures (workflow review stub PENDING REVIEW RE-IMPLEMENTATION, config catalog effort enum drift, project-memory evidence hash drift, store-child fixture trio, and others) that predate the story and need their own tracked issues; see commit 1a6d72e6e. The three failing shutdown-store-failure cases fail identically at the baseline; no shutdown or supervisor case was broken by the story, and the one shutdown-evidence scenario change is the story-mandated contract update (same class as t1's killed-owner rewrite).
